question: Generally in which month does the United Nations call its full General Assembly every year?
solution:
The correct answer is __**September**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) holds its annual session starting in **September**.
 
• This annual meeting is referred to as the "regular session" and typically begins on the third Tuesday of September.
 
• The session continues for a year but the most intensive part of the session, known as the "general debate," takes place in September and October.
 
• During the general debate, world leaders and representatives address the Assembly on a wide range of international issues.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **United Nations General Assembly (UNGA)**

 
 
• The UNGA is one of the six principal organs of the United Nations and the only one in which all member nations have equal representation.
 
• It serves as a forum for member states to deliberate and cooperate on international issues covered by the UN Charter.
 
• The UNGA addresses issues related to international peace and security, budgetary matters, and international law.
 
• Resolutions passed by the UNGA are non-binding but carry significant political weight and moral authority.
 
 
 
• **General Debate**
 
 
• The general debate is a high-level event where heads of state and government, along with other senior officials, present their views on pressing global issues.
 
• It provides a unique platform for world leaders to address the international community.
 
• Speeches delivered during the general debate often outline the foreign policies and international priorities of the participating countries.
 
• The general debate usually lasts for about nine days.
 
 
 
• **UNGA Sessions**
 
 
• In addition to the regular session, special sessions and emergency special sessions can be convened.
 
• Special sessions are called to address specific issues requiring immediate attention, while emergency special sessions are convened in cases of international crisis.
 
• The sessions are held at the UN Headquarters in New York City.
 
• Each member state has one vote, and decisions on important questions require a two-thirds majority.
